verdict.rationale: GitBook ships a first-party MCP server so agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor can create and configure sites, open change requests, draft content and edit pages, and its docs say you can "drive it from your agent." The first-party GitBook Agent also drafts improvements, but the evidence never shows it taking user commands, so natural-language operation relies mainly on an external agent client. Missing for 10: a documented in-product natural-language command interface, detail on which operations the GitBook Agent accepts by instruction, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Tools like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other MCP clients can use it to create and configure sites, open change requests, draft content, edit pages, and restructure docs.
Write in the editor, drive it from your agent, or sync from Git.
GitBook’s AI documentation agent identifies missing or outdated content, drafts improvements, and helps your team keep product knowledge aligned with real user needs
